title: Getting started with veryMAD
text: example uses small sequencing metadata table. Low library size low gene detection suggest poor complexity; high mitochondrial content also common QC concern. result keeps eight samples adds logical flag columns. Inspect columns matter quick review: mad_qc_outlier TRUE least one selected metric flagged. veryMAD remove rows, decision filtering follow-stays analysis workflow.
code: sample_metadata <- data.frame(   sample = paste0("sample_", 1:8),   library_size = c(2.4e6, 2.5e6, 2.6e6, 2.7e6, 2.8e6, 2.6e6, 0.45e6, 2.5e6),   detected_genes = c(12000, 12500, 13100, 12800, 13400, 12600, 1500, 12300),   pct_mito = c(.04, .05, .06, .05, .07, .06, .08, .29) )  # Describe which tail is a potential QC problem for each metric qc_directions <- c(   library_size = "lower",   detected_genes = "lower",   pct_mito = "upper" )  # Add one flag per metric and a combined flag to the metadata qc_annotated <- mad_qc(   sample_metadata,   metrics = qc_directions,   verbose = FALSE ) qc_annotated[, c("sample", "library_size_mad_outlier",                  "detected_genes_mad_outlier", "pct_mito_mad_outlier",                  "mad_qc_outlier")] #>     sample library_size_mad_outlier detected_genes_mad_outlier #> 1 sample_1                    FALSE                      FALSE #> 2 sample_2                    FALSE                      FALSE #> 3 sample_3                    FALSE                      FALSE #> 4 sample_4                    FALSE                      FALSE #> 5 sample_5                    FALSE                      FALSE #> 6 sample_6                    FALSE                      FALSE #> 7 sample_7                     TRUE                       TRUE #> 8 sample_8                    FALSE                      FALSE #>   pct_mito_mad_outlier mad_qc_outlier #> 1                FALSE          FALSE #> 2                FALSE          FALSE #> 3                FALSE          FALSE #> 4                FALSE          FALSE #> 5                FALSE          FALSE #> 6                FALSE          FALSE #> 7                FALSE           TRUE #> 8                 TRUE           TRUE

title: Getting started with veryMAD
text: Use output = "report" want thresholds flags compact object instead adding columns input table. threshold table records calculation status metric. Missing undersized metrics remain visible instead silently turned filtering decision.
code: qc_report <- mad_qc(   sample_metadata,   metrics = qc_directions,   output = "report",   verbose = FALSE )  qc_report$thresholds[, c("metric", "direction", "lower_raw",                          "upper_raw", "status")] #>           metric direction  lower_raw upper_raw status #> 1   library_size     lower 2105220.00        NA     ok #> 2 detected_genes     lower   10770.88        NA     ok #> 3       pct_mito     upper         NA  0.104478     ok qc_report$flags[, c("id", "mad_qc_outlier")] #>   id mad_qc_outlier #> 1  1          FALSE #> 2  2          FALSE #> 3  3          FALSE #> 4  4          FALSE #> 5  5          FALSE #> 6  6          FALSE #> 7  7           TRUE #> 8  8           TRUE

title: Robust MAD scaling
text: small vector represents expression summaries five genes. largest value easy see, determine centre scale . names preserved, missing values remain missing. Set center = FALSE scale = FALSE one part transformation needed.
code: gene_expression <- c(   gene_A = 8.2,   gene_B = 8.7,   gene_C = 9.1,   gene_D = 9.4,   gene_E = 18.0 )  scaled_expression <- mad_scale(gene_expression) round(scaled_expression, 2) #> gene_A gene_B gene_C gene_D gene_E  #>  -1.52  -0.67   0.00   0.51  15.01

title: Robust MAD scaling
text: matrix, margin = 1 scales rows margin = 2 scales columns. , rows genes columns samples, column scaling puts samples common robust scale. matrix dimensions dimnames preserved. zero MAD can handled zero_mad = "zero", "na", "error", depending result used downstream.
code: expression_matrix <- matrix(   c(     8.2, 8.5, 8.4, 8.6,     9.1, 9.0, 9.3, 9.2,     4.0, 4.2, NA, 4.1   ),   nrow = 3,   byrow = TRUE,   dimnames = list(     c("gene_A", "gene_B", "gene_C"),     c("sample_1", "sample_2", "sample_3", "sample_4")   ) )  scaled_by_sample <- mad_scale(expression_matrix, margin = 2) round(scaled_by_sample, 2) #>        sample_1 sample_2 sample_3 sample_4 #> gene_A     0.00     0.00    -0.67     0.00 #> gene_B     0.67     0.67     0.67     0.67 #> gene_C    -3.15    -5.80       NA    -5.06

title: Interpreting MAD QC flags
text: small table contains common sequencing QC metrics. One sample low complexity, one high mitochondrial content, one missing value. missing library size remains missing flag column. combined flag NA metric flagged least one metric evaluated. Review individual flags source metadata deciding sample.
code: qc_metadata <- data.frame(   sample = paste0("sample_", 1:7),   library_size = c(2.4e6, 2.5e6, 2.6e6, 2.7e6, 2.8e6, 0.5e6, NA_real_),   detected_genes = c(12000, 12500, 13100, 12800, 13400, 1600, 12200),   pct_mito = c(.04, .05, .06, .05, .07, .08, .30) )  qc_result <- mad_qc(   qc_metadata,   metrics = c(     library_size = "lower",     detected_genes = "lower",     pct_mito = "upper"   ),   verbose = FALSE )  qc_result$flags[, c("id", "library_size", "detected_genes",                     "pct_mito", "mad_qc_outlier")] #> NULL

title: Interpreting MAD QC flags
text: Count-like metrics can easier compare explicit transformation. threshold table keeps calculation-scale raw-scale limits. min_n computational safeguard. metric usable values, status insufficient_n; every value missing, status all_missing. statuses make limitation visible rather turning silent pass fail.
code: transformed_result <- mad_qc(   qc_metadata,   metrics = c(library_size = "lower", pct_mito = "upper"),   transform = c(library_size = "log1p"),   verbose = FALSE )  transformed_result$thresholds[, c(   "metric", "direction", "transform", "lower_raw", "upper_raw", "status" )] #> NULL

title: Interpreting MAD QC flags
text: zero MAD means usable values vary enough estimate non-zero robust spread. Choose policy matches downstream task. Use zero_mad = "na" leave flags unresolved, zero_mad = "error" zero spread stop workflow. stratified analyses, split data explicitly call mad_qc() subset. veryMAD infer batches, conditions, clusters, biological causes.
code: constant_metric <- data.frame(   sample = paste0("sample_", 1:6),   detected_genes = rep(12000, 6) )  zero_mad_result <- mad_qc(   constant_metric,   metrics = c(detected_genes = "lower"),   zero_mad = "zero",   verbose = FALSE )  zero_mad_result$thresholds[, c("metric", "mad", "lower_raw", "status")] #> NULL

title: veryMAD 0.5.1
text: Reduced exported API exactly mad_qc() mad_scale(). Removed mad_z_score() alias. Removed combine argument. mad_qc() now always returns overall mad_qc_outlier flag.

title: veryMAD 0.5.1
text: Added compact printing verymad_qc reports. Hardened empty-input, missing-value, identifier, overwrite, zero-MAD handling. Expanded tests complete public API important edge cases. Expanded continuous integration across Linux, macOS, Windows, multiple R versions.

title: veryMAD 0.5.1
text: Updated README vignettes final two-function interface. Simplified pkgdown reference index. Kept pak::pak("Thokas99/veryMAD") primary installation command.

title: veryMAD 0.5.0
text: Reduced public API mad_qc() mad_scale(). Removed grouped QC calculations separate modality workflows. Removed redundant per-result counts qualitative interpretation fields. Changed default QC transformation "none". Changed default zero-MAD policy "na".
